statBlock.specialAbilities:
Special Attacks: Improved grab, pounce, rake 1d3+1

Special Qualities: Low-light vision, scent

Imported from the d20 SRD; verify attacks and skills in-game. Full rules at d20srd.org.

system.biography:
These jungle cats are about 4 feet long and weigh about 120 pounds. They usually hunt at night. The statistics presented here can describe any feline of similar size, such as jaguars, panthers, and mountain lions.

Combat

Improved Grab (Ex)

To use this ability, a leopard must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can rake.

Pounce (Ex)

If a leopard charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex)

Attack bonus +6 melee, damage 1d3+1.

Skills

Leopards have a +8 racial bonus on Jump checks and a +4 racial bonus on Hide and Move Silently checks. Leopards have a +8 racial bonus on Balance and Climb checks. A leopard can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened. *In areas of tall grass or heavy undergrowth, the Hide bonus improves to +8.

system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Listen checks and Spot checks.

system.description: You are skilled at using light weapons.
system.benefit: With a light weapon, rapier, whip, or spiked chain made for a creature of your size category, you may use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier on attack rolls. If you carry a shield, its armor check penalty applies to your attack rolls.
system.special: Natural weapons are considered light weapons.

system.description: Check: You can walk on a precarious surface. A successful check lets you move at half your speed along the surface for 1 round. A failure by 4 or less means you can't move for 1 round. A failure by 5 or more means you fall.
Check: With each successful Climb check, you can advance up, down, or across a slope, wall, or other steep incline (or even a ceiling with handholds) at one-quarter your normal speed.
Make a Hide check to conceal yourself from enemies, slink past guards, slip away without being noticed, or sneak up on people without being seen or heard.
You can make running or standing jumps.
Your Listen check is either made against a DC that reflects how quiet the noise is that you might hear, or it is opposed by the target's Move Silently check.
Make a Move Silently check when you try to sneak past enemies or move without being heard.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.

What it does (SRD): In starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar dim lighting, the creature can see twice as far as a human can in the same light. It retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under those conditions that a human could not.

ThirdEra: Low-light vision is set on this item’s Details tab under Capability grants (vision and senses), not in Mechanical effects (no extra distance is needed for the usual reading of the rule). The character sheet includes it with other vision from items and race.

What it does (SRD): Scent lets the creature detect opponents by smell, usually out to about 30 ft. (strong scents farther, very weak scents closer). It can use scent to pinpoint a square once it is within 5 ft., and to track by Survival. Wind and water affect what it can smell.

ThirdEra: Scent (30 ft.) is set on this item’s Details tab under Capability grants (vision and senses), not in Mechanical effects. The character sheet includes it with other senses; Survival checks to track by scent still use the normal skill rules unless you add separate bonuses elsewhere.

What it does (SRD): If the creature charges, it can still make a full attack at the end of the charge (including rake attacks if listed).

ThirdEra: This is a full-attack pattern, not a numeric modifier here. Leave Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty unless you add a custom row. Resolve charge distance and attacks using the NPC sheet and combat tracker as usual.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits with a listed natural weapon, it can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. Details (size modifiers, opposed checks, holding vs pinning) follow the grapple rules.

ThirdEra: This template has no numeric rows in Mechanical effects or Capability grants. Track grapple state in play; use the NPC’s natural attacks and CMB/CMD from the sheet when resolving the grapple.

What it does (SRD): When the creature grapples or sometimes when it pounces, it can make extra natural attacks (usually two claw rakes) at the listed attack bonus against a grappled or appropriate target.

ThirdEra: Add rake attacks to the NPC’s Natural attacks list on the sheet (or note them in Description) so attack bonuses match the stat block. This template keeps Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty.
